title: Recession Watch
headline_read: No recession underway — but the warning lights are no longer all green.

indicators.title: Yield Curve · 10-Year minus 2-Year
indicators.context: The gap between 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields. When it goes negative (“inverts”), investors expect rate cuts ahead — and every U.S. recession since the 1970s was preceded by an inversion.
indicators.read: The curve recently un-inverted to +0.30 after an extended inversion. Recessions historically begin after the curve climbs back above zero — a reason for more vigilance, not less.

indicators.title: Sahm Rule Recession Indicator
indicators.context: A real-time recession alarm built from unemployment: it trips when the 3-month average jobless rate rises 0.5 points above its prior-year low. It has flagged every recession since 1970 with almost no false alarms.
indicators.read: The Sahm rule is at 0.43, climbing toward its 0.50 recession trigger but not there yet.

indicators.title: Initial Jobless Claims · weekly
indicators.context: How many people filed for unemployment benefits last week — the freshest read on layoffs. A sustained climb is one of the earliest signs of a weakening economy.
indicators.read: Initial jobless claims are low at ~219k — employers aren't shedding workers.

indicators.title: Unemployment Rate
indicators.context: The share of the labor force without a job and looking. A steady, sustained rise off its lows is a hallmark of an economy tipping into recession.
indicators.read: Unemployment at 4.2% is up 0.5 points from its recent low — the kind of rise that has preceded past downturns.
